title: Functions: parameters, results, and contracts
goal: Trace a function call and verify its promise about the result and state on rejection.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.while-do-while. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: Calls and definitions
paragraphs: If a sensor asks for a calculation and the result seems to disappear, locate the call. The function has an input, a return value and a caller that decides whether to store or print it.

In int twice(int value), twice names the function, the first int is the return type, and value is a local parameter. The body runs when called, not when the compiler encounters its definition. return 2*value finishes this invocation and supplies its result to the caller.

Define a teaching function before main so its declaration is visible at the call site. int result=twice(4) supplies the argument 4 and stores the result 8. Calling it does not print anything by itself; output is a separate operation.

sections.title: Values, references, and const
paragraphs: An int value parameter receives a separate value: changing it does not change the caller’s int. int& binds to the original object and permits mutation. const int& prevents mutation through that reference but neither copies the object nor makes it permanently const.
Small values usually travel by value. A large read-only object can be passed by const reference. A reference does not own its object, so never return a reference to a local variable.
In copied(original) the local parameter becomes 5, but original stays 4. After changed(original), the original object itself becomes 5. Compare the two output lines.

sections.title: Copy and mutation
paragraphs: Trace two calls with original = 4. In which one is the change visible to the caller?

sections.title: Preconditions and postconditions
paragraphs: The twice contract bounds its input so 2*value fits the type. That is straightforward for -1000 through 1000, but not for arbitrary int. A precondition is the caller’s obligation; a postcondition is the guaranteed result property when that obligation holds.

Do not treat malformed external input as a violation that can be ignored. At the boundary, main checks extraction and ranges before an internal function receives values. For an expected rejection, a bool result with an explicitly documented output parameter is useful.
A precondition is the caller’s obligation before a call, and a postcondition is what can be checked afterward. checkedArea checks both dimensions itself and promises to preserve result on rejection.

sections.title: Pure computation and side effects
paragraphs: A calculation function should not secretly read cin or change a global accumulator. The same arguments yield the same result without changing the environment. A unit test can then pass arguments directly and compare the result without replacing the console.

An output reference makes mutation visible in the signature but needs an exact rule: leave it unchanged on false. Calculate into a temporary and assign only on success. This is a simple form of operation atomicity.
Make rejection observable. Starting result at 17 lets false and 17 prove separate facts: the call rejected, and the output object stayed unchanged.

sections.title: Rejection without mutation
paragraphs: The first call gets −1 and 2. The second gets 3 and 4. Predict the flag and result after each call separately.

reveal.title: Reveal output and trace execution
paragraphs: The first line, 0 17, shows rejection without modification. The second, 1 12, shows successful assignment.

tables.caption: Trace for this run
rows: Both dimensions are valid, so the result is replaced.

sections.title: Decomposition without unnecessary coupling
paragraphs: Split the task into validation, calculation, and presentation. Each function should answer one question and have a meaningful name. Avoid ten unrelated parameters when one value suffices; a later struct will group related data.

Local variables in separate calls are independent. Returning a result by value is safe; returning a local object’s address is not. Recursion, authored templates, and overloading are unnecessary here and are not hidden lab requirements.
Keep cin extraction in main. Then checkedArea(-1, 2, result) can be tested without a stream by comparing the state before and after directly.

sections.title: Testing a function separately from input
paragraphs: Build an argument table: lower boundary, a normal value, upper boundary, and nearby rejections. Check that read-only operations leave the original object unchanged and that a false result preserves the output parameter.

Then add integration cases for cin: empty input, a wrong type, and an extra token. A successful unit test does not establish parser correctness. Next, pass a whole sequence to a function using the standard span view.
Test rejection after a success using the same result. Resetting it to zero before every call can hide an incorrect write on rejection.

sections.title: Now try your own task
paragraphs: The worked example calls the function from test code. Now connect it to a new input source: two values entered by a user. Preservation of result remains a separate function test.
Choose two different initial result values. For each, record what must remain when a dimension is negative.

selfcheck.prompt: Which output proves that rejection preserved 17 and the successful call replaced it?
feedback: Yes. Both flags and values match the contract.
Zero in the first line would mean rejection erased 17.
The first dimension is negative, so that call must return false.

selfcheck.prompt: What happens when an int is passed by value?
options: A reference to the original int is created
The parameter holds a separate value
selfcheck.feedback: Mutating the parameter does not mutate the original int.
This is an explicit function contract.

selfcheck.prompt: How can a parameter read a large string without copying?
selfcheck.feedback: The owner is alive during the call and mutation through the parameter is forbidden.

options: Ends the current call with a result
Ends all loops in all functions
selfcheck.feedback: Output and returning a result are separate operations.

selfcheck.prompt: What is needed to accept this lab?
options: Source, actual results, original tests, and a contract explanation
selfcheck.feedback: A progress flag is not evidence of independent mastery.

selfcheck.prompt: If result is already 12 after a successful call, what happens at checkedArea(-1, 4, result)? Why is invalid from main alone insufficient to prove result was preserved?
selfcheck.feedback: Place the one assignment to result after all dimension checks. A width of 0 is valid.

practice.title: Checked area at the input boundary
practice.task: Implement bool checkedArea(int w, int h, int& result). For dimensions in 0–1000, store their product and return true. On rejection, return false and preserve result. In main read exactly two integers. Print the area or invalid.
criteria: Compare 0 1000, 1000 1000 and 3 4 x. Separately call the function with invalid dimensions and demonstrate that result stayed unchanged.
A direct rejection test observes false and unchanged result=17; a valid 3×4 call observes true and 12.
Do not assign result before every check succeeds. Do not return a reference to a local variable.
Add two cases of your own, including a rejection if the interface allows one. Explain one boundary result.
Keep the source, exact input and observed output.
practice.hint: Place the one assignment to result after all dimension checks. A width of 0 is valid.

steps.action: Choose two different initial result values. For each, record what must remain when a dimension is negative.
steps.why: A nonzero initial value makes an accidental write on rejection visible.
steps.expected: Two trace rows for the same result: flag and value after a valid and an invalid call.

steps.action: Implement the function without cin or cout. Call it from main only after checking extraction and trailing input.
steps.why: The function has its own contract. It must also work in a test with no stdin.
steps.expected: The starter prints invalid for 3 4. After implementation, a successful call writes 12.

steps.action: Compare 0 1000, 1000 1000 and 3 4 x. Separately call the function with invalid dimensions and demonstrate that result stayed unchanged.
steps.why: The invalid message checks main's report, but not the state of the output parameter.
steps.expected: 0 1000 gives 0. A rejected call after success preserves the previous result.

terms.definition: an observable change beyond the return value.
an expression supplied in a function call.
a local input name in a function declaration.
an obligation before performing an operation.
a guarantee after an operation whose preconditions hold.
